transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I used to flinch when things fell. Now I just wait to see if they still have a pulse.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...I didn't see you standing there in the shadow.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Keep your voice down, boy, unless you want them to open the doors.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...Sorry. I didn't mean to make noise.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You have that look in your eyes. Like you fell down a very deep hole.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...I didn't fall. I walked in. But I can't find my way back.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I walked in too, forty years ago, and I stopped right here. The fountain is the one safe spot so I never step off the stone.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Forty years... how have you survived that long?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: By never being noticed. Head down, voice low, nothing that draws the houses. It keeps you alive and takes everything else.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...Tell me about the things watching from the houses.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: They are not curious about you. They are patient. The jinn don't move until something breaks the order — noise, light, a face that doesn't belong. You already broke two of those.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The ones in the windows... they felt heavy.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Say it quietly if you must say it at all — there is a king here. Ancient, the kind of old that has no number. He doesn't need to watch you himself — everything here is already his eyes.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I passed a woman at the gate who didn't blink.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: His daughter. Don't go back to that gate. Whatever she showed you in her face — it was a question, not a welcome. The wrong answer stays with you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...There are shapes in the bubbling pool. Pale hands.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't name them. They were people once but naming them wakes something in the water. Look away and keep walking.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...My brother Omar is down here because of me. I dared him to insult the well. A pale hand rose and took him before I could move.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Say the rest. Don't dress it up.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...It was my dare. He trusted me. That's all there is.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I made a mistake too, forty years ago, and no one helped me. Omar is kept, not lost — the king chose to hold him. That means he is still there.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...I know. And I am sorry you were alone.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Is there nothing here that fights back — that's what you want to ask.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...Yes. Is there.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is a light they fear. When it's called, the hands sink and the watchers go quiet — long enough to move. But using it is like lighting a flare in a cave.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...I don't mind the danger if it works.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My head pounds just reaching for it. The black surface stirs when I think about saying it out loud.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...Please. Give me a chance.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Why should I give you what I never used myself?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...Because you know what it costs to have no one give you anything when you needed it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I cannot show you the way out. The roads are gone from my head. I have nothing left that points anywhere.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...I don't need a map. I need the words.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The dark water is stirring. It knows what I am about to do. A window just went dark up there.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...Let it stir. Ring the bell, Hanash.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My jaw aches. The words ring loud in this square — everything in the dark will know where you stand.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...My name is Salim. Hold onto that while you say it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I am forgetting my own name. The well takes it when I help someone. That is the cost showing itself.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...Then say it before more is gone.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good. Now hold it — don't let it sit loud in your chest, just let it sit. The second is harder to give and harder to take back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...I'm ready.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...I have both. I won't let them go.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The first is a rope. The second is a torch. You use a rope before you light a torch, not the other way. The order matters more than the words.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...I understand.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: One last thing. If something speaks to you in a voice you almost recognize — stop. The dark is good at almost. It has had a long time to practice.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...I'll carry your name back to the sun, Hanash.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Just a man from the valley who never made it home. Say it where the light can hear it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: ...Stay strong.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I will try. You shouldn't die here. Find a better end than mine.
